1) reflex fluctuations between the arms and legs are not synchronous during rhythmic movement, and 2) the co-variabilty of bilateral reflex fluctuations is reduced by rhythmic limb movement, but only for the legs.
the modulation of spinal cord activity during voluntary contraction of the arms and leg cycling is not reflected by a common drive onto bilateral motoneuronal pools.
bilateral fluctuations of the Hoffmann (H)-reflexes are modulated by rhythmic movement of remote limb pairs.

the study of the neural control of rhythmic movements of the limbs.
the study of human motor control and the mechanisms that underlie the generation of rhythmic limb movements.

bilateral reflex fluctuations are influenced by the motor task, but not by the muscle group.
